scope: India-based clinical psychologists, psychiatric social workers, child & adolescent psychiatrists, family therapists, and court-attached counsellors verified from primary sources who satisfy at least one of: (a) peer-reviewed publication explicitly framing PA / PAS / parental alienating behaviours as a clinical or child-protection phenomenon; (b) named-on-record court appointment as counsellor / custody evaluator / expert in a reported India family court / HC / SC judgment turning on PA findings; (c) operates a PA-relevant reunification / co-parenting / high-conflict family intervention through a named institution; (d) publicly stated PA stance in named press / conference / primary-source practice-site article series.

stance_taxonomy.recognition: Treats PA / parental alienating behaviours as a real, assessable phenomenon; operates or endorses PA-specific reunification, expert-witness, or psycho-legal evaluation work; sourced via peer-reviewed publication or practice-site explicit statement
stance_taxonomy.critique: Argues PA construct is operationalised against DV / family-violence survivors; advocates DV / trauma-informed alternatives; sourced via publication or named-press statement
stance_taxonomy.middle: Engages both alienating-behaviour and family-violence frames; differential-diagnosis or court-attached differential practice; sourced via institutional mandate or court-engagement
stance_taxonomy.middle_leaning_recognition: Institutional middle position with personnel-overlap to PA-recognition publication line
stance_taxonomy.not_publicly_confirmed: Included for record-completeness; PA-specific stance not in primary sources

india_context_notes.regulation: No single national psychology licensing register. Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI) registers Clinical Psychologists under RCI Act 1992 via Central Rehabilitation Register (CRR) - https://www.rehabcouncil.nic.in/ . Psychiatric Social Work is not statutorily registered; credentialing flows through academic institutions (NIMHANS PSW, TISS) and the Indian Society of Professional Social Work. Psychiatry regulated under National Medical Commission Act 2019 (formerly MCI Act 1956); Indian Medical Register at https://www.nmc.org.in/information-desk/indian-medical-register/ . NIMHANS Bengaluru (deemed University under NIMHANS Act 2012) is the apex national child mental-health forensic/custody reference centre. IHBAS Delhi (autonomous body, established 1993 pursuant to SC PIL) is the apex North-India neuro-psychiatric institute and RCI-recognised MPhil Clinical Psychology trainer.
india_context_notes.apex_case: Lt Col Vivek Singh v Romani Singh, Civil Appeal 3962/2016, (2017) 3 SCC 231 - Bench Jasti Chelameswar J. and A.K. Sikri J., decided 13 February 2017. Judgment PDF https://main.sci.gov.in/judgment/judis/44566.pdf ; Indian Kanoon https://indiankanoon.org/doc/48721287/ . SC expressly defined 'The Parental Alienation Syndrome' and named on the record Ms Iti Kanungo, Principal Counsellor Family Court Patiala House New Delhi, as the court-appointed evaluator who submitted the psychological/sociological report dated 12 December 2016 on the child's preferences.
india_context_notes.subsequent_hc_pa_line: ABC v XYZ, 2023 SCC OnLine Del 6099 (Delhi HC, Suresh Kumar Kait J. and Neena Bansal Krishna J., October 2023) - PA from non-neglectful parent constitutes 'extreme act of mental cruelty' under HMA s.13(1)(ia) https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2023/10/01/delhi-hc-alienation-of-the-child-from-his-father-is-an-extreme-act-of-mental-cruelty-legal-news/ ; A v B, 2026 SCC OnLine Del 276 (Delhi HC, Anil Kshetarpal J. and Harish Vaidyanathan Shankar J., February 2026) - custody transferred on findings of 'sustained parental alienation' by mother https://www.scconline.com/blog/post/2026/02/02/del-hc-custody-to-father-parental-alienation/ . NO named mental-health expert appears on the record in either subsequent judgment.

Indian critique-camp positioning at present is institutional and women's-rights-organisation-led (CMHLP, Lawyers Collective WRI, CSR, TISS-CWCSW) rather than individual-clinician-led. Structural feature of the Indian field.

No identifiable NIMHANS court-appointed evaluator on Vivek Singh v Romani Singh on the public record despite NIMHANS being the natural national reference centre; only Iti Kanungo (Family Court Patiala House Delhi) is named.

No identifiable AIIMS Delhi PA-specific lead. Senior AIIMS faculty (Rajesh Sagar, Manju Mehta) have substantial child/adolescent and family-violence research lines but no PA-specific peer-reviewed publication located.

Indian Journal of Social Psychiatry 2026 case study 'A Case of Parental Alienation Syndrome in Custody Battle' (vol 42 issue 1, 63-65) is paywalled; authors not extractable from public-source search results.
RCI CRR numbers not enumerable in bulk; only name-by-state lookup at https://www.rehabcouncil.nic.in/ . Sharma's CRR number and other Tier-3 candidates' CRR numbers therefore not in this file.

Indian Medical Register (NMC India) numbers searchable but not displayed on most practice sites; specific MD-Psychiatry registration numbers for Astik Joshi, Chavda, Nisarga, Shetty not publicly displayed in practice / hospital profiles.

Court-counsellor profession in India falls under court-administrative appointment (Family Courts Act 1984) rather than a standalone regulated profession; Iti Kanungo's standalone psychology/social-work credentials and current incumbency not publicly confirmed.
